criteria: In search.py, `find_first(items, value)` returns the index of the first item equal to `value` in a list sorted in ascending order that may hold duplicates, or -1 if no item equals `value`.

In search.py, `find_last(items, value)` returns the index of the last item equal to `value` in a list sorted in ascending order that may hold duplicates, or -1 if no item equals `value`; for example, `find_last([1, 2, 2, 3], 3)` returns 3, not -1.
In search.py, `count_of(items, value)` returns how many items in a list sorted in ascending order that may hold duplicates equal `value`.

In search.py, `insert_position(items, value)` returns the index at which `value` can be inserted after any equal items so that the list stays sorted; for `[1, 2, 2, 3]` and 2 it returns 3, and for `[1, 2, 2, 3]` and 9 it returns 4.
All four functions (`find_first`, `find_last`, `count_of`, `insert_position`) work on the empty list, on a list of one item, and when `value` is smaller or larger than every item.
All four functions (`find_first`, `find_last`, `count_of`, `insert_position`) run in logarithmic time and do not walk the list.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
